iberia.description: Alfonso XIII’s Spain, shaken by the loss of Cuba (1898) and the Barcelona Tragic Week (1909), stays neutral in 1914. Portugal has been a republic since October 1910 and will enter the war in 1916. Genetics: continuity with emigration.

britain.description: Asquith’s Liberal government has curbed the Lords (1911) and passed Irish Home Rule, while Ulster unionists and Irish nationalists arm. Britain enters the war on 4 August 1914 after Germany invades Belgium. Genetics: continuity.

france.description: Poincaré’s France is allied with Russia and draws closer to Britain. Paris is the art capital of the world (Cubism, the Ballets Russes, Proust). Jaurès is assassinated on 31 July; Germany declares war on 3 August and the Marne halts the invasion in September. Genetics: continuity.

central.description: Germany, Europe’s strongest industrial economy, backs Austria-Hungary with the ‘blank cheque’ of 5 July 1914. Vienna, Budapest and Prague are capitals of modernism. Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia on 28 July. Genetics: continuity.

scandinavia.description: Norway has been independent since 1905; Sweden and Denmark declare neutrality in August 1914. Finland is a Russian grand duchy with its own parliament (elected by universal suffrage since 1906) under renewed Russification. Genetics: continuity.

italy.description: Italy, a member of the Triple Alliance, declares neutrality in August 1914 and will join the Entente in 1915 for Trentino and Trieste. The Libyan war (1911–12) and Futurism mark a restless young state. Genetics: continuity.

balkans.description: The Balkan Wars of 1912–13 divide Ottoman Macedonia and Thrace among Serbia, Greece and Bulgaria, and create Albania. Austria-Hungary, which annexed Bosnia in 1908, sees an enlarged Serbia as a deadly threat. Genetics: continuity with forced migration.

eastern.description: Nicholas II’s empire is industrialising fast, governed with a weak Duma after 1905. It mobilises in support of Serbia on 30 July 1914. The Ottoman Empire, run by the Committee of Union and Progress, signs a secret alliance with Germany on 2 August. Genetics: continuity.

GBR.ideas: New Liberalism: pensions (1908), national insurance (1911), the Parliament Act (1911).
GBR.literature: Conrad, Hardy, Shaw, E. M. Forster’s Howards End (1910); D. H. Lawrence’s Sons and Lovers (1913).
GBR.science: Rutherford’s nuclear model (1911); Moseley’s atomic numbers (1913).
GBR.story: On 3 August 1914 Grey tells the Commons why Britain cannot stand aside if Belgium is invaded; the ultimatum to Germany expires at 11 p.m. London time on 4 August.

IRL.art: Celtic Revival design; Jack B. Yeats.
IRL.ideas: Home Rule versus unionism; republican separatism.
IRL.literature: Yeats, Synge’s The Playboy of the Western World (1907), Joyce’s Dubliners (1914).
IRL.science: Harland & Wolff, Belfast, builders of the Titanic (1912).
IRL.story: In September 1914 Home Rule becomes law and is suspended in the same breath; Redmond urges the Volunteers to fight for Britain, splitting the movement that will rise at Easter 1916.

FRA.art: Picasso and Braque’s cubism; Matisse; Delaunay.
FRA.literature: Proust’s Swann’s Way (1913); Apollinaire’s Alcools (1913); Alain-Fournier’s Le Grand Meaulnes (1913).
FRA.science: Marie Curie’s second Nobel Prize (1911); Poincaré’s mathematics.
FRA.story: On 29 May 1913 Stravinsky’s The Rite of Spring, danced by the Ballets Russes in Nijinsky’s choreography, provokes uproar at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées.

ESP.art: Gaudí’s Sagrada Família; Picasso’s Barcelona beginnings.
ESP.literature: Unamuno’s Niebla (1914); Antonio Machado’s Campos de Castilla (1912).
ESP.philosophy: José Ortega y Gasset’s Meditaciones del Quijote (1914).
ESP.science: Santiago Ramón y Cajal, Nobel Prize 1906.
ESP.story: When the army calls up Catalan reservists for Morocco in July 1909, Barcelona rises; churches burn in the Tragic Week and the anarchist educator Ferrer is executed.

PRT.literature: Fernando Pessoa and Mário de Sá-Carneiro prepare Orpheu (1915).
PRT.science: Egas Moniz’s early career in Lisbon.
PRT.story: The revolution of October 1910 sends King Manuel II into exile in England and ends almost eight centuries of monarchy.

NLD.science: Kamerlingh Onnes discovers superconductivity (1911; Nobel 1913); Lorentz.
NLD.story: The Peace Palace in The Hague, funded by Andrew Carnegie, opens on 28 August 1913, home of the Permanent Court of Arbitration—a year before the war.

BEL.story: On 2 August Germany demands passage; Albert refuses. Leuven’s university library burns on 25–26 August, becoming a symbol of the war on civilians.

DEU.literature: Thomas Mann’s Death in Venice (1912); Rilke; Stefan George.
DEU.science: Max Planck; Einstein moves to Berlin in 1914; Haber–Bosch ammonia.
DEU.story: On 5 July 1914 Wilhelm II and Bethmann Hollweg promise Austria-Hungary German backing against Serbia—the ‘blank cheque’ that turns a Balkan crisis into a European war.

AUT.art: Klimt’s golden period; Schiele; Adolf Loos; Schoenberg’s atonality.

images.alt: Freud and colleagues at Clark University, 1909
images.caption: Freud and colleagues at Clark University, 1909

AUT.literature: Karl Kraus’s Die Fackel; Schnitzler; Hofmannsthal.
AUT.story: Vienna sends Serbia an ultimatum on 23 July 1914 designed to be rejected, and declares war on 28 July.

HUN.story: Tisza at first opposes war with Serbia, fearing more Slavs in the monarchy; by 14 July he gives way.

CZE.art: Mucha; the Municipal House (1912); Janáček’s Jenůfa (1904).

images.alt: Mucha at work on the Slav Epic
images.caption: Mucha at work on the Slav Epic

CZE.science: Škoda Works, Plzeň, the monarchy’s arsenal.
CZE.story: In December 1914 Masaryk leaves Austria and begins the campaign abroad for an independent Czechoslovakia.

BIH.literature: Young Bosnia’s poets; later Ivo Andrić.
BIH.story: On 28 June 1914 the archduke’s car takes a wrong turn near the Latin Bridge; Gavrilo Princip shoots Franz Ferdinand and his wife Sophie.

POL.literature: Henryk Sienkiewicz, Nobel Prize 1905; Reymont’s The Peasants (1904–09).
POL.philosophy: Positivism and Young Poland modernism; Kazimierz Twardowski’s Lwów school of logic.
POL.story: On 6 August 1914 Piłsudski’s First Cadre Company crosses from Austrian Galicia into Russian Poland.

RUS.art: Kandinsky, Goncharova, Malevich; Stravinsky’s Rite of Spring.

images.alt: Chamber of the State Duma, Tauride Palace
images.caption: Chamber of the State Duma, Tauride Palace

RUS.story: St Petersburg is renamed Petrograd in August 1914 to sound less German.

images.alt: Gallen-Kallela, The Defence of the Sampo (1896)
images.caption: Gallen-Kallela, The Defence of the Sampo (1896)

FIN.story: In 1907 Finland elects the world’s first women members of parliament: 19 of 200 seats.

UKR.story: Russia bans the centenary of Taras Shevchenko’s birth in 1914.

SWE.art: Carl Larsson’s domestic idylls; Anders Zorn.
SWE.ideas: Parliamentarism versus royal power; universal male suffrage (1909).
SWE.literature: Selma Lagerlöf, first woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1909); August Strindberg.
SWE.philosophy: Ellen Key’s writings on childhood and women’s rights.
SWE.science: The Nobel Prizes, awarded in Stockholm since 1901; Svante Arrhenius.
SWE.story: On 6 February 1914 some 30,000 farmers march to Stockholm Palace; in the Courtyard Speech Gustaf V promises them stronger defences, against his Liberal government. Karl Staaff resigns and a non-party ministry under Hjalmar Hammarskjöld takes over.

NOR.art: Edvard Munch, whose murals for the University of Oslo’s Aula are installed in 1916.
NOR.ideas: Women gain the vote in national elections in 1913.
NOR.literature: Knut Hamsun; Sigrid Undset’s early novels.
NOR.science: Polar exploration: Nansen and Amundsen; Kristian Birkeland’s aurora research.
NOR.story: Roald Amundsen reaches the South Pole on 14 December 1911.

DNK.art: Vilhelm Hammershøi’s quiet interiors; Carl Nielsen’s symphonies.
DNK.ideas: Neutrality and a new democratic constitution (1915), giving women the vote.
DNK.literature: Henrik Pontoppidan (Nobel Prize 1917); Johannes V. Jensen.
DNK.story: In 1913 Niels Bohr, back in Copenhagen from Rutherford’s Manchester laboratory, publishes his model of the atom with electrons in fixed orbits.

CHE.literature: Carl Spitteler’s ‘Our Swiss Standpoint’ speech (December 1914) calls for neutrality of the heart.
CHE.philosophy: Ferdinand de Saussure (d. 1913); Carl Jung breaks with Freud (1913).
CHE.story: Einstein publishes special relativity in 1905 while at the Bern patent office.

ITA.art: Umberto Boccioni and Giacomo Balla’s Futurist painting.
ITA.ideas: Irredentism: Trentino and Trieste still Austrian.
ITA.literature: Gabriele D’Annunzio; Luigi Pirandello; Grazia Deledda.
ITA.story: Marinetti’s Futurist Manifesto appears on the front page of Le Figaro on 20 February 1909, praising speed, machines and war as ‘the world’s only hygiene’.

SRB.ideas: Yugoslav unity; the secret ‘Black Hand’ in the officer corps.
SRB.philosophy: Liberal and radical political thought around Pašić.
SRB.science: Mihajlo Pupin and Nikola Tesla abroad; Mihailo Petrović Alas in Belgrade.
SRB.story: At Cer in August 1914 the Serbian army defeats the Austro-Hungarian invasion.

GRC.art: Neoclassical Athens of Ziller and the Hansens.
GRC.ideas: The Megali Idea of uniting all Greeks.
GRC.literature: Constantine Cavafy in Alexandria; Kostis Palamas.
GRC.philosophy: The ‘language question’: demotic Greek against katharevousa.
GRC.science: The National and Kapodistrian University of Athens.
GRC.story: Under the 1913 Treaty of Bucharest Greece gains Thessaloniki and southern Macedonia; its territory and population grow by about two-thirds.

BGR.ideas: San Stefano Bulgaria and the claim to Macedonia.
BGR.literature: Ivan Vazov’s Under the Yoke; Peyo Yavorov.
BGR.story: In June 1913 Bulgaria attacks Serbia and Greece over Macedonia; Romania and the Ottomans join in, and by the Treaty of Bucharest it loses most of its gains.

ROU.ideas: Union of all Romanians, including Transylvania.
ROU.literature: Mihail Sadoveanu; George Enescu’s Romanian Rhapsodies (music).
ROU.story: At the Crown Council of 3 August 1914 King Carol I, a Hohenzollern, wants war beside Germany; his ministers refuse. He dies on 10 October.

ALB.art: Shkodër photography studio of the Marubi family.
ALB.literature: Naim Frashëri’s national poetry; the Latin-based alphabet adopted at Manastir (1908).
ALB.philosophy: Sami Frashëri’s programme for an Albanian state.
ALB.science: The first Albanian schools and the standard alphabet of 1908.
ALB.story: Wilhelm of Wied lands at Durrës in March 1914; facing a peasant revolt and the outbreak of war, he leaves in September.

TUR.art: First National Architectural style (Vedat Tek, Mimar Kemaleddin).
TUR.literature: Ömer Seyfettin’s short stories; the ‘National Literature’ movement.
TUR.story: On 29 October 1914 the Ottoman fleet, led by the German battlecruiser Goeben, shells Russia’s Black Sea ports, bringing the empire into the war.

MNE.ideas: Union with Serbia versus the Petrović dynasty.
MNE.literature: Petar II Petrović-Njegoš’s The Mountain Wreath (1847).
MNE.story: In 1913 Montenegro captures Scutari (Shkodër) after a long siege, then has to hand it over to the new Albania under great-power pressure.
